clue.text: Show superiority, as ceramic thief does?

definitions.meaning: to outclass someone thoroughly, beat them hands down
read as three words, a thief of ceramics 'knocks' (steals) pots and makes 'off' with them

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about how a pottery thief shows off.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer differently and a thief who knocks (British slang for steals) pots goes off with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to beat or outshine someone comprehensively, a display of clear superiority.

clue.text: Finding idle amusement — perhaps shooting bird

parts.note: shooting is one example of slaying, so killing
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, time

explanation.surface: A pastime, such as shooting at birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like the target of the shooting, but it is slang for a spell in prison (rhyming slang: bird-lime = time).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means passing hours idly with some diversion while waiting.

clue.text: Amerindian not starting a quantity of medicine

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a measured amount of medicine is a dosage

explanation.surface: A Native American who goes without his first dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, now based in Oklahoma.

clue.text: Last of hock, say, and very cold fizz

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
bitter weather is very cold

explanation.surface: Wine drinkers pick a chilled sparkling drink after their hock.
explanation.walkthrough: Keg bitter is a British draught beer served chilled and carbonated from a pressurised keg, hence the fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizz here is a loose term for any carbonated drink, and this pressurised beer is notably gassy.

clue.text: Run wearing clog, for example

indicators.note: wearing means the clog goes around the run, like a garment

parts.note: a patten is a wooden-soled overshoe, a kind of clog
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A dancer runs in clogs for a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or exemplar to copy, so an example to follow.

clue.text: Captured a card, tossing in two higher ones

indicators.note: tossing in means adding the next items into the middle of the card

parts.note: a ten is a playing card
ace and king are cards ranking above a ten, A and K

explanation.surface: A card game where a trick is won by throwing in two better cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken is a past participle meaning seized or captured.

clue.text: Start of lunch, once cook's made ready?

definitions.text: Start of lunch, once cook's made ready?

indicators.note: made ready signals the letters being prepared, put into a new order
start of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the possessive s is not counted, just cook

explanation.surface: Lunch begins once the chef has prepared the food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the traditional lunch hour starts at this time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain lunch traditionally begins at one in the afternoon.

clue.text: Cry of dismay as celebration's halved

indicators.note: halved means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a fiesta is a festive celebration

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disappointment when the party is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word; only the first half of FIESTA is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: This old exclamation expresses disgust or reproach, a cry of dismay.

clue.text: Half-amusing excuse

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: amusing in the sense of pleasing or entertaining

explanation.surface: A half-hearted, slightly funny excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a pretext offered in defence, an excuse.

clue.text: With India's tail in, get slips to ring man at wicket

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the rearranged word
slips signals that the letters slide into a new order
tail means just the final letter of the word

parts.note: a keeper is a ring that holds another ring in place

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: an Indian batsman edges to the slips and the keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' rearranges GET to GTE, A goes inside to make GATE, and 'to' is a link word. The cricket surface misleads: a wicket is also a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small gate, so the man stationed at one is a gatekeeper.

clue.text: Brown covering for this dynamic chap

definitions.meaning: in UK mains wiring the live conductor is sheathed in brown insulation

explanation.surface: A Brown who covers for an energetic colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the colour of insulation on the live conductor in British electrical wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an energetic, vivacious person.

clue.text: Kissed her soundly? That's sweet

indicators.note: soundly means the phrase is heard, not read

parts.note: to neck is to kiss, so kissed her is necked her

explanation.surface: He kissed her heartily, and how sweet it was.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with no final R, 'necked her' is said like the answer. 'That's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sweet liquid of flowers, or any delicious drink.

clue.text: A doctor taking grains, sealing envelope: how much is wanted initially?

indicators.note: sealing means the first pieces close around the envelope
taking means the doctor takes on the grains next

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
rice is a cereal grain
a skin is an outer covering or envelope

explanation.surface: A doctor sealing up some rice in an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealing' puts the envelope inside the rest, just after the A; 'taking' joins the doctor to the grains. The definition is the price a seller asks at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: The asking price is the sum a seller wants at the start of negotiations.

clue.text: Say, in country roads can these appear?

definitions.text: Say, in country roads can these appear?

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: in means the can is placed inside the country roads

parts.note: lanes are narrow country roads
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A question about which flowers might be found along country lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: these wild roses grow in country hedgerows.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose of hedgerows beside country lanes.

clue.text: A girl keeping pounds in investment — that looks fair

indicators.note: keeping means the girl holds the next piece inside

parts.note: she stands for a girl or woman

indicators.note: in means the pounds are put inside the investment

parts.note: a bond is a fixed-interest investment
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A girl puts her money into investments that look fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts pounds inside the investment, making BLOND, and 'keeping' has the girl hold that; 'A' comes first. 'fair' here means light-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde is a pale greyish hair colour, so someone who looks fair.

clue.text: I've secured brig —— maybe star prisoner inside

indicators.note: inside means the prisoner is placed within the star

parts.note: a shiner is something that shines, such as a star
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Someone who has secured a brig, perhaps with a star prisoner aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A brig is a sailing ship, so whoever has acquired one can say this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has acquired a brig, a two-masted sailing vessel, owns a ship.

clue.text: Acceptable to turn over centre of wood here

indicators.note: turning over the centre means the middle two letters swap places

parts.note: acceptable means all right, okay

explanation.surface: It is acceptable to turn over the middle of this wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle pair of OKAY is turned round, giving AK in place of KA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaky describes wine tasting of the oak casks, so of wood in character.

clue.text: Express sorrow, having limited vision

indicators.note: limited means the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: vision means eyesight, sight

explanation.surface: Someone with poor eyesight expressing sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigh is a long audible breath that expresses sadness or regret.

clue.text: Lock girl in at sea, being boisterous

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl locked in on board ship, behaving riotously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollicking means exuberantly lively and noisy, boisterous.

clue.text: Throw energy into request, having asked for support

parts.note: to lob is to throw in a high arc

indicators.note: into means energy goes inside the request

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or request

explanation.surface: Putting energy into a request after asking for backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to petition influential people for support, so lobbied means asked for it.

clue.text: Roughly grabbed around centre of gallows, in turn one may hang by the neck

definitions.text: one may hang by the neck

indicators.note: in turn means the whole assembly is read backwards
around means the grabbing goes about the central letter

parts.note: pawed means handled or grabbed clumsily

indicators.note: centre of means only the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gruesome execution image, with someone roughly seized and hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: PAWED around L gives PALWED, which 'in turn' reverses. The gallows surface is a grim misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewlap is the loose fold of skin hanging from the throat of cattle or other animals.

clue.text: Proper old piano part

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper

explanation.surface: A correct, old-fashioned part for the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the primo is the upper part, played by the first pianist.

clue.text: Missile launcher, one alight perhaps on British base

indicators.note: on means the next piece sits after the others

parts.note: base means low, mean
a pipe is one thing that is lit, for example

explanation.surface: A missile launcher set up on a British base with someone lighting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the lit thing after British and base. A blowpipe fires darts, hence missile launcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which darts are blown, so a missile launcher.

clue.text: Make hole, working spike

parts.note: to pit is to make a hole or depression
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: Drilling a hole with a working spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike driven into rock by climbers.

clue.text: In St Trinian, worked out oxygen is a sort of element

indicators.note: in means the oxygen goes inside the rearranged school name
worked out means the letters are re-solved into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A school chemistry lesson at St Trinian's on oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: St Trinian's is a fictional unruly British girls' school. 'worked out' makes TRANSITIN, and O goes inside; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Transition elements are the metals of the central block of the periodic table, a sort of element.

clue.text: Parting words eliciting tear?

definitions.meaning: the epitaph rest in peace, abbreviated, said on parting from the dead
to tear is to rend or split

explanation.surface: Farewell words that bring on a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliciting' is a link word; 'tear' is the verb to rend, not a drop of weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation on gravestones is a parting phrase, and the word also means to tear.

clue.text: Labour play will be broadcast

indicators.note: be broadcast means the words are heard, not read

parts.note: to toy is to play, so play will becomes toy'll

explanation.surface: A Labour play to be shown on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but it is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil means hard, exhausting labour.

clue.text: In majority of force copper earned nothing at first for work

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a new order
at first means only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: In a majority, a forceful police officer earned nothing at first for his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is British slang for a police officer, not the metal. 'In' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Preponderance means superiority in weight or number, a majority of force.
